text: What does the Boyd-Chua (1985) theorem guarantee, providing the theoretical license for reservoir computing?
choices: Only linear time-invariant functionals can be approximated, and only by linear reservoirs
Any causal, time-invariant fading-memory functional can be approximated to arbitrary accuracy by a finite-dimensional driven dynamical system plus a readout
Fading-memory functionals can be approximated only if the recurrent weights are trained by gradient descent
Approximation always requires an infinite-dimensional state, ruling out practical reservoirs
explanation: Boyd-Chua extends Stone-Weierstrass to functionals: any causal, time-invariant fading-memory functional is approximable to within any epsilon by a finite-dimensional driven system with a readout. It is not restricted to linear functionals, needs no training of the recurrent dynamics, and requires only finite (not infinite) state dimension.
